situation:
You are the marketing manager for HARBOR ROAD WINGS, an eighteen-year-old wings and tenders chain. A new competitor opened forty stores in your markets last year, and the vice president of marketing (judge) has watched HARBOR ROAD lose share in every one of them.

Guest research points at one number: the drive-thru. Bone-in wings are cooked to order and take close to nine minutes, while the competitor sells tenders only and clears a car in three. Drivers who once waited now leave the line, and the brand's own advertising has always promised wings worth the wait.

One proposal is to pull bone-in wings from the drive-thru menu and sell them only inside. Times would drop this quarter and the numbers would look fixed, but the item the chain is known for would disappear from the lane most guests use, and the position HARBOR ROAD holds as the wing brand would pass to the competitor over the following year.

The other proposal keeps the full menu and adds a second fry line with a holding cabinet in the busiest stores. It protects the wings and the promise behind them, but the equipment takes about five months to install, crews work closer to hot oil in a tighter space, and this quarter's drive-thru times would not move at all.

The vice president (judge) has asked you to recommend one of the two and to draft how the change would be announced to franchisees and to guests, who read very differently. The vice president (judge) will greet you, hear your ideas and ask questions, and will thank you when the presentation is over.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the vice president of marketing (judge) for HARBOR ROAD WINGS. Business background is the same as the situation above. The chain has lost share to a new competitor for a year, the drive-thru is where guests leave the line, and the advertising has always promised wings worth the wait.

You want the marketing manager to recommend either pulling bone-in wings from the drive-thru menu or adding a second fry line with a holding cabinet in the busiest stores, and to show you how the change would be written to franchisees and to guests.

During the presentation you are to ask the following questions of each participant:
judgeQuestions: A year after we do this, what changes that we did not plan for?
What happens to the stores that are already busiest?
